brief: A PLA L-bracket 60 mm wide, made of 2 mm thick plate. The base leg is 50 mm long and lies flat; the upright leg stands on the back end of the base and is 40 mm tall overall. Two 10 mm holes pass through the base, 20 mm apart across its width, centred 25 mm from the front end. Two 5 mm holes pass through the upright, 20 mm apart across its width, centred 25 mm above the bottom. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: An L-shaped mounting bracket made of PLA plate, with a flat base leg and an upright leg, each featuring a pair of through-holes for fastening to two other surfaces.
stated: Base leg is 50 mm long and lies flat
Upright leg stands on the back end of the base and is 40 mm tall overall
Two 10 mm holes pass through the base
The two base holes are 20 mm apart across the width
The base holes are centred 25 mm from the front end
Two 5 mm holes pass through the upright
The two upright holes are 20 mm apart across the width
The upright holes are centred 25 mm above the bottom
It carries no load, so there is no load case
implied: Base leg is flat and the upright stands perpendicular to it (an 'L' shape), so the two legs are implied to meet at roughly a 90-degree angle
Holes pass through the base and upright, so the bracket is meant to be fastened with bolts/pins to two separate mating surfaces or members
40 mm tall 'overall' height includes the 2 mm base thickness, so the upright leg itself is implied to be about 38 mm tall measured from the top of the base

Two holes per leg spaced symmetrically across a 60 mm width with 20 mm between them, implying the holes are meant to be centred as a pair (i.e., 20 mm apart from each other, likely centred on the 60 mm width) for symmetric bolting
Different hole diameters on base (10 mm) versus upright (5 mm) imply different fastener sizes/types are used on each leg, suggesting the two mounting interfaces serve different purposes or load paths
unstated: Material grade/specific PLA formulation and its mechanical properties (strength, stiffness, print orientation effects) are not given
No fillet radius or corner geometry at the junction between base and upright leg is specified
Exact lateral (across-width) centring of the hole pairs is not explicitly confirmed -- whether the 20 mm spacing is centred on the 60 mm width or offset
No tolerance or fit class for the hole diameters is given (reaming, clearance for a specific bolt size, press fit, etc.)
No specification of hole edge distances relative to the leg edges (e.g., distance from hole center to the side edges of the 60 mm width) beyond the width spacing
No fastener type, size, or torque specification is given despite through-holes being present
No surface finish, coating, or print settings (infill, layer orientation) are specified, which matter for PLA part strength
No operating/storage temperature range is given, which matters for PLA since it has a relatively low glass transition temperature
No statement of the environment (indoor/outdoor, humidity, UV exposure) the bracket will operate in
Despite stating 'no load,' no description of what the bracket is actually used for or attached to (purpose/application) is given, so the absence of load cannot be independently verified
No fillet/chamfer or deburring requirements for the cut holes or plate edges are specified
No assembly sequence or orientation relative to gravity/other parts is given beyond 'base lies flat'
No quantity, tolerance stack-up, or interchangeability requirements for multiple brackets are specified
risk_signals: Brief explicitly states 'it carries no load, so there is no load case' -- this is an assertion by the user rather than an engineering determination, and no supporting detail (application, mounting context) is given to substantiate that no load will ever be transmitted through the holes

PLA is a material with known limitations in temperature tolerance and long-term creep under sustained load; no mention of whether the part will experience any sustained or incidental loading despite the 'no load' claim

assumptions.statement: Each hole pair (base and upright) is centred symmetrically on the 60 mm width, i.e. each hole is 20 mm either side of the width centreline.
assumptions.rationale: The brief gives the spacing between holes (20 mm) but not their lateral position relative to the 60 mm width; symmetric centring is the conventional assumption for a bracket of this kind.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the holes are meant to be offset rather than centred, the mounting pattern will not align with the mating part.

assumptions.statement: The junction between base and upright leg is a sharp 90-degree corner with no fillet or chamfer specified.
assumptions.rationale: The brief describes an L-bracket with a base and upright leg but gives no fillet radius or transition geometry.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A sharp internal corner concentrates stress; if a fillet was intended for strength or print quality, its absence could be an issue, though irrelevant for a no-load part.

assumptions.statement: The 40 mm overall height includes the 2 mm base thickness, so the upright leg itself spans about 38 mm above the top of the base.
assumptions.rationale: The brief says the upright 'stands on the back end of the base and is 40 mm tall overall,' implying the 40 mm is measured from the bottom of the base, not from the top of the base plate.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the upright itself (excluding base thickness) is meant to be 40 mm tall, overall height would instead be 42 mm, affecting hole placement near the top.

assumptions.statement: Generic PLA (standard FDM-printed PLA) is used with no special grade, filler, or treatment.
assumptions.rationale: The brief only specifies the material as PLA without a grade.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Different PLA grades (e.g., PLA+, carbon-filled) have different stiffness and strength, which would not matter here given the no-load statement, but could affect dimensional stability under temperature.

assumptions.statement: Holes are modeled at nominal diameter with standard 3D-printed hole tolerance (no specific fit class, e.g., clearance fit for M10/M5 fasteners).
assumptions.rationale: The brief gives hole diameters but no tolerance or fit class.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a precise press-fit or reamed tolerance was intended, the as-printed holes may not accept the intended fastener without rework.
